q: 我们现在住的房子___旧，想换一套新___的。
zh: 我们现在住的房子有点儿旧，想换一套新一点儿的。
py: wǒ men xiàn zài zhù de fáng zi yǒu diǎn r jiù xiǎng huàn yī tào xīn yī diǎn r de
en: The house we live in now is a bit old; we want to swap it for a slightly newer one.
why: The state of the current house is 有点儿旧 (before the adjective); the desired change is 新一点儿的 (after it). 一点儿旧 and 新有点儿 are not Chinese.

q: 今天比昨天暖和___，不用穿那么厚。
zh: 今天比昨天暖和一点儿，不用穿那么厚。
py: jīn tiān bǐ zuó tiān nuǎn huo yī diǎn r bù yòng chuān nà me hòu
en: Today is a bit warmer than yesterday; you don't need to dress so thickly.
why: With 比 the difference goes after the adjective: 暖和一点儿. 有点儿 and 很 cannot appear in a 比 sentence in this position.

q: 小王说的话我___也没听懂。
zh: 小王说的话我一点儿也没听懂。
py: xiǎo wáng shuō de huà wǒ yī diǎn r yě méi tīng dǒng
en: I didn't understand any of what Xiao Wang said.
why: 'Not any at all' of a past event is 一点儿也没 + verb. 有点儿 and 一些 cannot be followed by 也没.

q: 司机师傅，前面的路不太好走，请您开慢___。
zh: 司机师傅，前面的路不太好走，请您开慢一点儿。
py: sī jī shī fu qián miàn de lù bù tài hǎo zǒu qǐng nín kāi màn yī diǎn r
en: Driver, the road ahead is rough going; please drive a bit more slowly.
why: A polite request for slower driving is verb + adjective + 一点儿. 一下 would count the action, not the degree, and 有点儿 cannot follow 慢.

q: 我今天___都不累，还想再走一会儿。
zh: 我今天一点儿都不累，还想再走一会儿。
py: wǒ jīn tiān yī diǎn r dōu bù lèi hái xiǎng zài zǒu yī huì r
en: I'm not tired at all today; I even want to walk a little longer.
why: 一点儿都不累 means 'not tired at all'; 有点儿 is never part of this frame, and the continued wish to walk shows 'not at all'.

q: 地铁站在前面，你走快___，我们要迟到了。
zh: 地铁站在前面，你走快一点儿，我们要迟到了。
py: dì tiě zhàn zài qián miàn nǐ zǒu kuài yī diǎn r wǒ men yào chí dào le
en: The subway station is up ahead; walk a bit faster, we're going to be late.
why: Urging someone to speed up is a request for change, so 一点儿 follows 快. 有点儿 would only describe a state and cannot follow the adjective.

zh: 我今天有点儿累。
py: wǒ jīn tiān yǒu diǎn r lèi
en: I'm a bit tired today.
why: 有点儿 goes directly before the adjective 累. The time word may come before or after 我, but 有点儿 cannot follow 累.

q: 我想喝___水，你有吗？
zh: 我想喝一点儿水，你有吗？
py: wǒ xiǎng hē yī diǎn r shuǐ nǐ yǒu ma
en: I'd like to drink a little water; do you have some?
why: 'A little of something' is 一点儿 + noun after the verb. 有点儿 cannot sit between a verb and its object, and 一下 counts actions, not amounts.

s: 妈妈有点儿不放心，所以一直给我打电话。
zh: 妈妈有点儿不放心，所以一直给我打电话。
py: mā ma yǒu diǎn r bù fàng xīn suǒ yǐ yī zhí gěi wǒ dǎ diàn huà
en: Mom is a bit uneasy, so she keeps calling me.
why: 有点儿 can stand before 不 + a positive word (不放心) to mean 'a bit uneasy'. It looks odd to learners but it is a normal pattern.

en: This piece of clothing is a bit unsuitable; try something else.

why: The current state gets 有点儿 before 窄; the comparison gets 一点儿 after 宽. 有点儿 can never trail the adjective, and 一点儿 can never lead it.

q: 外面___吵，我听不清你说什么。
zh: 外面有点儿吵，我听不清你说什么。

q: 妹妹___不高兴，因为妈妈不让她看电视。

s: 这件毛衣一点儿大，有没有小一点儿的？
zh: 这件毛衣有点儿大，有没有小一点儿的？

q: 这个问题有点儿难，让我想___，明天再告诉你好吗？

q: 这条路___远，我们打车去吧。
